text:
Authentication & Authorization
Auth is centralized in **auth-service**, not shared-secret HS256 between api-gateway/user-service as before:

- **auth-service** issues RS256 (asymmetric) JWTs, keyed off its own private key, publishes public keys at `/.well-known/jwks.json`. Issuer `https://auth-service`, audience `ms-code-execution`, access token TTL 15 min, refresh token TTL 14 days.
  - `POST /auth/register`, `/auth/login`, `/auth/refresh` — end-user auth
  - `POST /auth/token` — OAuth2 client-credentials grant for machine-to-machine calls (submission-service authenticating to problem-service to fetch a problem's harness; ai-analysis-service authenticating to submission-service/problem-service when triggered by Kafka). Allowed clients are configured in `service-clients.clients.*` (e.g. `submission-service`, `ai-analysis-service`, role `SERVICE`). `worker-service-go` authenticates to nothing — it calls no other service directly.
  - Calls user-service over **gRPC** (port 9090) to look up/verify users during login.
- Every other business service (api-gateway, user-service, problem-service, submission-service, execution-result-service, ai-analysis-service) is **independently an OAuth2 resource server** — each validates JWTs itself against auth-service's JWKS/issuer/audience, rather than trusting the gateway alone.
- **user-service** owns user CRUD and roles only. `AdminBootstrap` idempotently seeds one ADMIN account on startup (`ADMIN_EMAIL`/`ADMIN_PASSWORD` env vars). `PATCH /users/{email}/role` (ADMIN-only) promotes other users.
- **IDOR fix**: `submission-service`'s `GET /submissions/{id}` is scoped by `findByIdAndUserId` and returns 404 (not 403) on mismatch to avoid confirming existence to an attacker. `GET /submissions/user/{userId}` requires the JWT subject to match the path `userId`.
- `POST /problems/{id}/harness/regenerate` is gated ADMIN-only via `@PreAuthorize` on `ProblemService.regenerateHarness` — same defense-in-depth pattern as `createProblem` (route-level rule allows any USER/ADMIN through `/problems/**`, the method-level check narrows to ADMIN).
- ⚠️ **`problem-service`'s `GET /problems/**` route requires `hasAnyRole("USER", "ADMIN", "SERVICE")`, not just `USER`/`ADMIN`.** `submission-service`'s `HarnessApplier` fetches `GET /problems/{id}` (for `harnessByLanguage`) using its own service-credential token — `/internal/**` doesn't expose harness data, only test-cases/limits, so this general route is the only place to get it. Narrowing this to drop `SERVICE` (it looks redundant if you only check what *problem-service itself* references) breaks every submission in production — confirmed by doing exactly that on this branch and catching it only via a real end-to-end submission test, not code review. `GET /problems/{id}/testcases` stays ADMIN-only regardless, via its own `@PreAuthorize` on `ProblemService.getTestCasesForWorker` — that method-level check is the actual hidden-test-case gate, independent of this route-level rule.
title: Authentication & Authorization

text:
Multi-language judging (LeetCode-style harness system)
The platform judges "LeetCode-style" submissions (`class Solution { ... }` / a plain function, not a full stdin/stdout script) by generating language-specific boilerplate — a **harness** — from an admin-authored, language-agnostic function signature, and gluing it to the user's submitted code before it's judged.

**Currently supported: Python, Java, C++, C, JavaScript, TypeScript, Go** — 7 languages total. A problem with no signature at all still works as a raw stdin/stdout script judge (the original, pre-harness behavior), for both this and every future language.

**Where things live:**
- `problem-service`'s `harness/` package: one `HarnessGenerator` implementation per language (`PythonHarnessGenerator`, `JavaHarnessGenerator`, `CppHarnessGenerator`, `CHarnessGenerator`, `JavaScriptHarnessGenerator`/`TypeScriptHarnessGenerator` — these two delegate to shared `JsFamilyHarness` logic since JS/TS output is nearly byte-identical, `GoHarnessGenerator`). Adding a new language is registering one new `@Component` implementing `HarnessGenerator` — nothing else needs to change structurally.
- `Problem.harnessByLanguage`: a single `Map<String,String>` column (language id → generated code), persisted as JSON via `HarnessMapConverter` — NOT one column per language. `ProblemService` autowires `List<HarnessGenerator>`, indexes it by `language()`, and loops over it to populate the map at problem-creation time.
- `POST /problems/{id}/harness/regenerate` (ADMIN-only): re-runs every *currently-registered* generator against a problem's already-stored signature, overwriting `harnessByLanguage`. This is how an existing problem picks up a language added after it was created — call it once per problem whenever a new `HarnessGenerator` ships.
- `submission-service`'s `HarnessApplier`: looks up `harnessByLanguage.get(lang)`, prepends a small per-language `PREAMBLES` entry when the language needs one (Java: `import java.util.*;`; C++: `#include <bits/stdc++.h>`/`using namespace std;`; C: stdio/stdlib/string/stdbool/ctype includes; Go: `package main` + its harness's required imports — Python/JS/TS need no preamble), then appends the harness. Falls back to the user's code unchanged if there's no harness for that language.
- `worker-service-go` executes per-language via a small registry rather than hardcoded branches: `sandbox.go`'s `buildLangDescriptors`, a `map[domain.Language]*langDescriptor` — image, optional two-step compile+exec commands, source filename, optional extra `Env`.

**Per-language sandbox images** (see `worker-service-go/internal/config/config.go`'s `LanguageImages`):

| Language | Image | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Python | `python:3.12-slim` | interpreted, no JSON helper needed (`json` stdlib) |
| Java | `eclipse-temurin:21-jdk-alpine` | compiled; hand-rolled `__Json` helper appended (`JsonHelper.java.txt`) — no JSON lib in a plain JDK sandbox |
| C++ | `gcc:14` | compiled; hand-rolled `__json` namespace (`JsonHelper.cpp.txt`) |
| C | `gcc:14` | compiled; hand-rolled `__json_*` functions (`JsonHelper.c.txt`); real LeetCode-C signature convention (raw pointers + `numsSize`/`returnSize` out-params), not a custom struct vocabulary |
| JavaScript | `node:20-slim` | interpreted; `JSON.parse`/`JSON.stringify` built in, no helper needed |
| TypeScript | `platform/node-typescript:20` (**locally built**) | compiled (`tsc`) then run with `node`; no official image ships both Node and `tsc`, and the sandbox has no network access to `npm install` it at request time — **must be built once**: `docker build -t platform/node-typescript:20 infra/sandbox-images/node-typescript`, then imported into whatever runtime actually schedules the sandbox pods (Kubernetes' own containerd, e.g. `docker save platform/node-typescript:20 \| ctr -n k8s.io images import -` for k3s — this image has no registry to pull from, so kubelet can't fetch it any other way; see `infra/k8s/README.md`) |
| Go | `golang:1.22-alpine` | compiled (`go build`); `encoding/json` stdlib handles both parse and serialize via an anonymous struct — no hand-rolled JSON helper needed at all, unlike C/C++/Java |

⚠️ **gcc has no `-slim` tag on Docker Hub** — only bare version tags (`gcc:12`, `gcc:14`, ...). `gcc:14-slim` doesn't exist and will 404.

⚠️ **Go's sandbox compile step sets `GOMAXPROCS=1`/`GOFLAGS=-p=1`** (via `langDescriptor.Env`, passed as `corev1.EnvVar` entries on the pooled pod's container spec in `podspec.go` — previously a generic `-e KEY=VAL` Docker CLI passthrough) — without it, `go build` compiling the full stdlib dependency chain from a cold, per-submission `GOCACHE` spawns enough concurrent compiler/assembler subprocesses to blow through the pids ceiling (fork-bomb protection; now a node-wide kubelet `--pod-max-pids` rather than a per-container Docker `--pids-limit` — see the "sandbox execution mechanism runs on Kubernetes" note above), failing every submission with "resource temporarily unavailable". Also needs `GOCACHE`/`HOME` pointed at a writable path (`/tmp`) since the sandbox's non-root user has no real `$HOME`.

⚠️ **TypeScript needs an inline `declare function require(id: string): any;`** ambient declaration in the generated harness (TS-only, JS's generated code is otherwise identical) — a standalone, no-project `tsc <file>.ts` invocation has no way to discover `@types/node` (global npm installs aren't on its default `typeRoots` lookup), so `require`/`fs` are otherwise unresolvable.

⚠️ **The legacy Java worker's `DockerExecutionService` only pulls an image if it isn't already present locally** (`inspectImageCmd` first, `pullImageCmd` only on `NotFoundException`) — required for `platform/node-typescript:20`, which exists only in the local Docker daemon, never on any registry; an unconditional pull 404s on it.

**Run vs Submit:** `SubmissionRequest.includeHidden` (boolean, defaults to `true`/full-Submit semantics unless explicitly `false`) — `false` judges only the problem's visible/sample test cases (LeetCode's "Run Code"), `true` judges everything including hidden cases ("Submit"). Threaded through `SubmissionCreatedEvent` (Kafka), the worker filters its test case list accordingly before judging. **Every test case is always judged and reported — the worker never short-circuits on the first failure** (an earlier design that stopped at the first failing case was deliberately changed).

**Per-test-case result reporting:** the worker reports a structured `TestCaseResult[]` (ordinal, passed, hidden, and `input`/`expected`/`actual` — populated only for non-hidden cases, a hidden test case's content is never sent anywhere past the worker) rather than a single flat output string.
title: Multi-language judging (LeetCode-style harness system)

text:
Inter-Service Communication
**Synchronous (REST):**
- API Gateway routes via load balancer (`lb://SERVICE-NAME`) using Eureka service discovery
- auth-service ↔ user-service via gRPC (port 9090)
- `worker-service-go` calls neither problem-service nor submission-service — submission-service embeds everything a job needs into the Kafka event it publishes
- submission-service calls problem-service (also via OAuth2 client-credentials) to fetch a problem's generated harness before publishing to Kafka
- execution-result-service uses OpenFeign declarative clients

**Asynchronous (Kafka) — a single pipeline:**
- `submissions.created.v1` (submission-service → worker-service-go, code uploaded to S3/MinIO first, test cases/limits embedded inline) → `execution-result-topic` (worker-service-go → execution-result-service — the single ingestion point for judged results)
- `execution-result-service` fans out two lightweight events: `submission-update-topic` (→ submission-service, flips its `status` column) and `analysis.trigger.v1` (→ ai-analysis-service, which auto-runs its LLM analysis; has its own `analysis.trigger.v1.retry-1`/`retry-2`/`.dlq` topics for retry/failure handling)
- worker-service-go additionally publishes failed messages to `dlq.submissions.created.v1`, and infra-level failures to `executions.failed.v1`

Kafka now runs SASL_SSL only (no plaintext listener), with AclAuthorizer and default-deny ACLs. Topics/ACLs are provisioned by the `kafka-init` one-shot container via `infra/kafka/acls.sh`.

**Eureka service names:** `USER-SERVICE`, `AUTH-SERVICE`, `PROBLEM-SERVICE`, `SUBMISSION-SERVICE`, `EXECUTION-RESULT-SERVICE`, `SOLUTION-SERVICE`, `AI-ANALYSIS-SERVICE`, `WORKER-SERVICE-GO`
title: Inter-Service Communication

text:
API Gateway Routes
All external traffic enters via port 8080:
- `/auth/**` → AUTH-SERVICE
- `/users/**` → USER-SERVICE
- `/problems/**` → PROBLEM-SERVICE (includes `POST /problems/{id}/harness/regenerate`)
- `/submissions/**` → SUBMISSION-SERVICE
- `/api/results/**` → EXECUTION-RESULT-SERVICE
- `/solutions/**` → SOLUTION-SERVICE

There is currently **no gateway route for ai-analysis-service** (no `/ai/**` entry) — call it directly on port 8000 if the route hasn't been re-added.
title: API Gateway Routes

text:
Solution Service
Backs the Solve page's "Solutions" tab (written explanation + step-through visualizer) — not yet wired to the frontend, which still reads a hardcoded `frontend/src/data/solutions.ts` for this content.

- `GET /solutions/problem/{problemId}` (USER/ADMIN) — a `Solution`'s parts (each stored as its own `SolutionPart` row: `ordinal`, `title`, `markdown` — not one giant blob, so the frontend can fetch/render each "Part N" bullet independently and an admin can edit one without touching the rest) plus `visualizerUrl` if a visualizer has been uploaded.
- `POST /solutions` (ADMIN) — full-replace upsert: swaps every part for a `problemId` with exactly the list in the request body.
- `POST /solutions/problem/{problemId}/visualizer` (ADMIN, multipart) — uploads a self-contained visualizer HTML file to MinIO/S3 (bucket `platform-solution-assets`, key `solutions/{problemId}/visualizer.html`); `Solution.visualizerObjectKey` points at it. Markdown text lives in Postgres, the visualizer blob does not — same "blob content goes in MinIO, not a TEXT column" split submission-service and problem-service already use.
- `GET /solutions/problem/{problemId}/visualizer` — streams that HTML back with `Content-Type: text/html`. Deliberately **unauthenticated** (permitted at both solution-service's own `SecurityConfig` and api-gateway's `SecurityConfig`) since it's loaded directly by a browser `<iframe src="...">`, which has no way to attach a Bearer token; visualizer content isn't sensitive. Not a presigned MinIO URL — MinIO's container hostname (`minio`) isn't resolvable from the browser, only from other containers on the compose network, so the service proxies the bytes itself instead.
title: Solution Service

text:
Code Execution (worker-service-go)
- Launches sandbox Pods through the Kubernetes API (in-cluster ServiceAccount token, or `K8S_IN_CLUSTER=false`+`KUBECONFIG_PATH` for local dev) — no `/var/run/docker.sock` mount, no Docker CLI, not part of `docker-compose.yml` at all. See the "sandbox execution mechanism runs on Kubernetes" note above and `infra/k8s/`.
- Execution timeout: 30 seconds; compilation gets a proportionally longer timeout (`max(3× wall timeout, 15s floor)`) — cold tsc/go-build startup overhead is otherwise roughly constant regardless of a fast problem's short execution budget.
- Test cases and judging limits are embedded into the `submissions.created.v1` event by submission-service (see "`worker-service-go` is the only worker" note above) — the worker does not call problem-service itself. Compares actual vs. expected output for PASSED/FAILED/TLE/MLE/RE/CE/SYSTEM_ERROR verdicts.
- Test-case content and submission artifacts are stored in MinIO/S3 (buckets `platform-test-cases`, `platform-artifacts`), provisioned by the `minio-init` one-shot container
- See "Multi-language judging" above for how a submission's raw code becomes the actual thing that gets compiled/run
- The only HTTP surface this service has at all: `GET /healthz` (liveness, 200 once the process is up) and `GET /readyz` (readiness, 200 once the Kafka consumer goroutine has started) on `HEALTH_PORT` (default `8091` - `8090` is already kafka-ui's host port) — added for Kubernetes probes, since otherwise this is a pure Kafka consumer with nothing else to point a probe at
title: Code Execution (worker-service-go)

text:
Databases
PostgreSQL, one database per service: `user_service`, `auth_service`, `problem_service`, `submission_service`, `execution_result_service`, `solution_service`, `ai_analysis_db`. Provisioned by `infra/postgres/init-multiple-databases.sh`.

- **Schema management is now Flyway (`db/migration/V1__init.sql`, `V2__...`, `V3__...` per service), `ddl-auto=validate`** — NOT Hibernate auto-DDL (`update`) as before. Add new migrations rather than relying on Hibernate to alter the schema. `problem_service` is up to `V3__harness_by_language.sql` (replaced per-language `harness_python`/`harness_java` TEXT columns with a single `harness_by_language` JSON column).
- Each Java-service DB has two roles: an **owner** role (DDL, used only by Flyway) and an **app** role (DML-only, used by the running service).
- `ai_analysis_db` is the exception — no Flyway equivalent for SQLAlchemy, so it connects directly as owner.
- All connections require TLS (`sslmode=verify-full`); Postgres accepts `hostssl` only, no plaintext auth.
title: Databases

text:
AI Analysis Service (Python)
FastAPI service with:
- Groq LLM for code analysis, via `litellm` (`services/llm_provider.py`) — provider-agnostic `<provider>/<model>` naming, model swappable via `LLM_MODEL`/`LLM_FALLBACK_MODEL` env vars with no code change.
  - ⚠️ **Groq's available-model list is account-specific and shifts under you.** The original defaults (`groq/llama-3.1-8b-instant`, `groq/llama-3.1-70b-versatile`) both broke in production — one decommissioned outright by Groq, the other returning "does not exist or you do not have access to it" for this account despite still being listed on Groq's own public docs page. This was completely silent: submissions exhaust both retry tiers, land in the DLQ, and `GET /ai/analysis/{id}` just hangs at `PENDING` forever with no error surfaced anywhere. Currently pinned to `groq/openai/gpt-oss-20b` / `groq/openai/gpt-oss-120b`, verified against the real key via `GET https://api.groq.com/openai/v1/models` (not Groq's public docs — that listed models this key doesn't actually have). If AI analysis silently stops working again, check this first, the same way, before assuming it's a code bug.
- pgvector (Postgres-backed, via `langchain_community.vectorstores.PGVector` in `services/rag_service.py`) for RAG context — migrated off a local ChromaDB directory; `infra/postgres/init-multiple-databases.sh` creates the `vector` extension as superuser at DB init.
- Registers itself with Eureka (`py-eureka-client`)
- Independently verifies incoming JWTs as an OAuth2 resource server (`security/jwt_verifier.py`, PyJWT + `PyJWKClient` against auth-service's JWKS, checking issuer/audience) — no longer a "header just has to be non-empty" check
- Caches analysis results in PostgreSQL
- `GET /health` for K8s liveness/readiness; graceful shutdown via FastAPI's `lifespan` (cancels the Kafka consumer task, deregisters from Eureka, disposes the DB engine) — see the `FastAPIInstrumentor` timing gotcha under "Infrastructure Hardening" below before touching `main.py`'s startup sequence.

Infrastructure Hardening (`infra/`)
`infra/kafka/` and `infra/postgres/` contain local-dev TLS/ACL bootstrapping (certs, JAAS config, `pg_hba.conf`, init scripts) — no Terraform/Kubernetes/nginx. Note: CA/server/broker private keys are committed here for local-dev convenience; do not reuse these certs in a real deployment.

`infra/sandbox-images/node-typescript/` holds the Dockerfile for the locally-built TypeScript sandbox image (see "Multi-language judging" above) — the only sandbox image that isn't pulled straight from Docker Hub.

The Kafka admin password is not yet env-driven (hardcoded in `infra/kafka/kafka_server_jaas.conf` / `admin-client.properties`) — flagged in-repo as a follow-up (Vault or similar).

`infra/otel/otel-collector-config.yaml` configures a minimal OTel Collector (traces only, OTLP in → OTLP out to Jaeger). `ai-analysis-service` and `worker-service-go` export to it (`otel-collector:4317`/`4318` inside the compose network); Jaeger UI at `:16686`, in-memory storage only (no Elasticsearch/Cassandra — traces don't survive a `jaeger` restart). The other 9 Java services aren't instrumented, so there's no full-request tracing across the whole platform yet, only across these two hops.

⚠️ **Python's `OTLPSpanExporter` only auto-appends `/v1/traces` when it reads `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` itself** — passing `endpoint=` explicitly to its constructor (as `ai-analysis-service/tracing.py` does) bypasses that, so the path has to be appended manually or every export 404s. Go's `otlptracehttp.WithEndpoint` doesn't have this problem (it always appends the path itself) — this is a real, confirmed difference between the two SDKs' APIs, not a copy-paste inconsistency.

⚠️ **`FastAPIInstrumentor.instrument_app(app)` must run before the ASGI app receives its first call, not inside a `lifespan` startup handler.** Starlette caches `app.middleware_stack` on the very first `__call__` (which is the `lifespan` scope invocation itself) — a middleware added during that same lifespan's startup handler is added too late to affect the already-built, cached stack, so every request traces zero spans with no error anywhere. Confirmed by reproducing it directly. `ai-analysis-service/main.py` calls `configure_tracing(app)` immediately after `app = FastAPI(...)`, not inside `lifespan()`.
